## Patient-Led Research Collaborative

Scores draw on peer-reviewed articles [@davis2021; @mccorkell2021;
@fitzgerald2024], the original preprint [@davis2020preprint] and the
collaborative's research-fund page [@plrc_fund]. Patients chose the questions,
designed and ran the survey, analysed the data and wrote every paper, and a
patient panel allocated USD 4.8 million in research grants, so every Domain A
stage was scored as led (●) and the case is classed as extreme citizen science.
Its first report on Long COVID appeared in 2020, before most clinical studies
(C2 = ●). The verdict is partial rather than success because, although patients
influenced definitions and guidance, direct adoption of the collaborative's own
findings is not documented (C3 = ◐).
